text: The mineral belt is marked on the map. Extraction, fuel, and processing are interdependent; none can be skipped.

Hydro, wind, and biomass can all power small generators. Choose the local grid route without mining or burning coal for power.
Grounding, circuit breakers, and regular inspections make power a reliable public service; once complete, you can establish an electricity and communications office.
Permanent radio stations have taken over the messengers' legwork. Intercity departures require an on-duty dispatcher and a reliable power supply, rather than repeated manual requests.
Medical staff use medicine and power to vaccinate residents while on duty; public health begins to shift from treating illness to preventing it.
Recycled scrap iron is machined into standard mechanical parts; the public route can also produce parts locally without forcing mining.

An electrified freight network and dispatch center now link the old stations; one-way trips for new freight orders along the lakeshores between the two cities have fallen from 180 seconds to 45 seconds. Freight, travel rations, return trips, and onboard drivers are still allocated by the rules.
Allocate power based on stock levels and minimum public needs; workshops switch to automated batching, and the administration can manage Old Town's daily schedules.
